To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a combination of chiral and achiral Lewis basic catalysts results in an exceptionally high increase in the facility (i.e., rate) of catalytic enantioreactive monosilylations, without loss of selectivity.
the addition of an achiral nucleophile to a chiral Lewis basic catalyst promotes enantioselectively catalyzed reactions of alcohols with trimethylsilyl chloride.
a counterintuitively designed combination of Lewis basic catalysts can promote the enantioselectively silyl protection of polyols with a remarkable rate enhancement, without loss of selectivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for catalytic enantiospecific synthesis, particularly in the area of organosilicon chemistry.
the development of new catalytic enantiospecific reactions that are applicable to a variety of organic substrates and provide access to synthetically useful molecules.
the development of new methods for the synthesis of chiral compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a Lewis basic co-catalyst, which is not necessarily the same as the chiral catalyst, is essential for achieving high reactivity and enantioselectivities in the silylation of alcohols.
the achiral co-promoter acts to accelerate the catalytic process by increasing the concentration of active chiral species in the reaction medium.
the combination of a chiral and an achiral Lewis basic catalyst is a new and effective approach to the catalytic enantiospecific monosilylation of polyhydric alcohols.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of a chiral and an achiral Lewis basic catalyst is a highly effective strategy to promote enantioselectively silyl-protecting alcohols.

we have found that a combination of seemingly competitive nucleophiles and bases can work in concert such that the achiral nucleophilicity promotes reaction, while the chiral Lewis base catalyzes enantioselectivization.
the addition of a Lewis base to a chiral Lewis basic catalyst can be a powerful way of enhancing reaction rates and enantiomercial purities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

seemingly competitive Lewis basic catalysts can work in concert such that an achiral Lewis basic catalyst serves as a nucleophilic co-catalyst and a chiral Lewis basic catalyst acts as a Brønsted acid catalyst.
the presence of a Lewis basic co-catalyst can be used to enhance the activity of the chiral catalyst.
the combination of a chiral and achiral Lewis base catalyst can lead to an unexpected synergy that can be exploited to accelerate reactions and improve their enantiomeric selectivity.
